changeSet.author: hms
changeSet.comment: Optimistic locking on Bed. Assigning a bed is the one place in Phase 2 where two people genuinely race for the same row: two nurses putting two patients into the same free bed at the same moment. Without a version column one of them silently wins and the bed holds two patients, which is not a state anything can recover from.

changeSet.author: hms
changeSet.comment: A bed number is unique within its ward, not across the hospital: ward A and ward B may each legitimately have a bed 1.

changeSet.author: hms
changeSet.comment: One admission per visit. The entity models this as a ManyToOne because a unidirectional relationship keeps the generator away from Phase 1's hand-tuned entities, so the one-to-one-ness is enforced here instead of by a JPA annotation.

changeSet.author: hms
changeSet.comment:
One patient in a bed at a time — expressed as a partial index so that the same bed can be reused by the next admission, and so that the bed a discharged patient occupied stays recorded on their admission rather than being cleared.
Note what is deliberately NOT here: "one open admission per patient". The patient is reached through the visit (Admission has no patient column, so that the identity merge has one fewer reference to carry), and a partial unique index cannot join. That invariant is therefore enforced in the admission service instead — recorded in phase2.md, slice 3, because it is a rule the database cannot hold for us.

changeSet.author: hms
changeSet.comment: At most one ACTIVE payment plan per bill. A bill may accumulate plans over time — one that defaulted and was renegotiated — so the constraint is partial rather than unique on bill_id. Two plans that are both "the agreement we are working to" would make the discharge gate ambiguous.
